2609.29781.title: Hallucination Neurons and Where to Find Them: An Investigation into the existence of Hallucination Neurons
2609.29781.paper_summary: Interpretable machine learning for Large Language Models (LLMs) increasingly relies on sparse probing methods that identify small sets of neurons claimed to detect and causally influence behaviors such as factuality recall, safety alignment, and hallucination. These claims have important implications for model auditing and behavioral steering, yet they are rarely tested against known failure modes of $L_1$-regularized probing in correlated, high-dimensional feature spaces. We propose a five-step diagnostic protocol covering feature correlation, bootstrap stability, sparse versus dense ranking disagreement, intervention baselines, and cross-dataset evaluation as a minimum standard for sparse-neuron localization claims. We investigate prior work using our proposed approach, specifically on H-neurons using open-source LLMs across TriviaQA, BioASQ, and NQ-Open datasets. Our results demonstrate detection replicates across both models and datasets, and exceeds the original reported AUROC gaps for TriviaQA and BioASQ datasets. Gemma 3 4B consistently outperforms MedGemma 4B on matched datasets, with AUROC gaps of +0.311 versus +0.235 on TriviaQA, +0.474 versus +0.455 on BioASQ, and +0.128 versus +0.112 on NQ-Open respectively. Causal validation at $n = 500$ with five random seeds shows statistically significant effects beyond random same-layer baselines. At the same time, the diagnostic results indicate that the selected neurons are not uniquely localized. Across the three Gemma 3 4B settings, 19 of 22 selected H-Neurons have Pearson $|r| > 0.7$ with other features, bootstrap selections show only moderate stability, and sparse and dense rankings overlap only weakly. Our findings show that sparse predictive structure can coexist with non-unique neuron selection. Routine diagnostic validation is necessary to distinguish detection claims from localization claims in mechanistic interpretability.
2609.29781.paper_summary_zh: 可解釋的機器學習對大型語言模型（LLMs）的依賴日益增強，尤其是稀疏探測方法，這些方法識別出聲稱能夠檢測並因果影響行為（如事實回憶、安全對齊和幻覺）的少量神經元。這些聲稱對模型審核和行為引導具有重要意義，但它們很少針對已知的$L_1$正則化探測在相關的高維特徵空間中的失效模式進行測試。我們提出了一個五步診斷協議，涵蓋特徵相關性、自助穩定性、稀疏與密集排名不一致、干預基準和跨數據集評估，作為稀疏神經元定位聲稱的最低標準。我們使用我們提出的方法調查了先前的研究，特別是在使用開源LLMs的TriviaQA、BioASQ和NQ-Open數據集上對H神經元的研究。我們的結果顯示，這兩個模型和數據集之間的檢測重複，並且超過了TriviaQA和BioASQ數據集原始報告的AUROC差距。Gemma 3 4B在匹配數據集上的表現始終優於MedGemma 4B，TriviaQA上的AUROC差距為+0.311對+0.235，BioASQ為+0.474對+0.455，NQ-Open為+0.128對+0.112。以$n = 500$進行的因果驗證，使用五個隨機種子顯示出超出隨機同層基準的統計顯著效果。同時，診斷結果表明所選的神經元並不是唯一定位的。在三個Gemma 3 4B設置中，22個選定的H神經元中有19個與其他特徵的Pearson $|r| > 0.7$，自助選擇顯示出只有中等穩定性，而稀疏和密集排名僅弱重疊。我們的發現表明，稀疏預測結構可以與非唯一神經元選擇共存。常規診斷驗證是必要的，以區分機械可解釋性中的檢測聲稱和定位聲稱。
